label: Proposed Master's research
title: Experience-Driven Character Evolution
workingTitle: A Shared Experience Model for Adaptive Behaviour and Skill Progression in RPG Companion Agents
summary: A proposed RPG research prototype in which a shared representation of accumulated gameplay experience guides both companion behaviour adaptation and skill progression.
statusNote: This page describes a proposed research direction. It does not report a completed implementation, experiment, or research result.

sections.label: Research vision
sections.title: One history, two forms of character evolution.
paragraphs: The proposed research explores whether characters that begin from the same initial state could evolve differently according to their actual gameplay histories. A shared Character Experience Profile would represent accumulated encounters, combat events, choices, and conditions in a structured form.

The same profile would be consumed by both a companion behaviour system and a skill-progression system, so changes in behaviour and abilities remain connected to what the character has experienced rather than appearing as unrelated or random variation.

sections.label: Character Experience Profile
sections.title: Structured gameplay history, not unrestricted narrative.
paragraphs: Gameplay events and combat metrics could be transformed into a shared representation that captures relevant patterns over time. The profile would provide a common, inspectable basis for adaptive behaviour and skill progression.

cards.title: Observed actions
items: Attack, defence, support, and movement patterns

cards.title: Designer-facing representation
cards.body: The proposed profile would remain structured and interpretable so designers can define what signals matter and how they may affect character development.

sections.label: Two consumers
sections.title: Behaviour and skills evolve from the same experience.
paragraphs: The key concept is not a separate behaviour model and skill generator working independently. Both systems would refer to the same accumulated experience, allowing a companion's decisions and abilities to develop as related outcomes of its play history.

cards.title: Behaviour adaptation
cards.body: A companion could gradually adjust tactical preferences, support choices, positioning, or responses to recurring situations.

cards.title: Skill progression
cards.body: Skills could develop through structured progression rules that reflect established experience patterns and designer-defined limits.

cards.title: Character divergence
cards.body: Characters with matching starting states but different conditions could gradually diverge in explainable ways that remain tied to their histories.

sections.label: Designer control
sections.title: Adaptation inside authored boundaries.
paragraphs: The proposal treats adaptation as part of an authored game system. Deterministic logic, constraints, balance rules, and observable boundaries would remain central so that change is understandable and controllable rather than unconstrained.

cards.title: Rules and constraints
cards.body: Designers could specify permitted behaviour changes, skill progression conditions, and boundaries for the game world.

cards.title: Balance and stability
cards.body: Evaluation would consider whether changes remain consistent, stable over time, and appropriate to the intended gameplay conditions.

cards.title: Explainability
cards.body: The shared profile could make it possible to relate a character change back to recorded experience and defined game rules.

sections.label: Research aim
sections.title: A focused RPG companion-agent prototype.
paragraphs: The proposed prototype would serve as an experimental environment rather than a complete commercial RPG. Its purpose would be to study whether one shared experience representation can support adaptive companion behaviour and skill progression while preserving designer control.

flow.model:
Shared Experience Model
Character Experience Profile

researchQuestions: Can a shared representation of accumulated gameplay experience guide both companion behaviour adaptation and skill progression so that characters evolve in ways that reflect their actual gameplay histories?
To what extent can behaviour changes and skill progression remain aligned with the experience patterns represented in a Character Experience Profile?
Can characters with the same initial state diverge meaningfully under different gameplay conditions while remaining within designer-defined constraints?
How stable and explainable are adaptive changes over time within repeated or comparable gameplay conditions?
How do players perceive character evolution when behaviour and abilities develop from a shared history?

comparison.title: A — Fixed Companion and Skill Tree
comparison.body: Behaviour and abilities follow predetermined authored paths.

comparison.title: B — Separate Adaptive Systems
comparison.body: Behaviour and skill changes use separate inputs or rules without a shared experience representation.

comparison.title: C — Shared Experience Model
comparison.body: Both behaviour adaptation and skill progression are informed by one structured Character Experience Profile.

comparisonNote: A future evaluation could consider experience–behaviour alignment, skill–experience alignment, character divergence, within-condition consistency, temporal stability, player perception, and rule compliance. These are proposed evaluation dimensions, not reported results.

scope.title: Game space
items: Defined encounter conditions and gameplay events
A limited set of authored skills and behaviour options

scope.title: Boundaries
scope.body: The initial prototype would prioritise a controlled, observable research environment over a complete RPG, autonomous-agent claim, or production-scale companion system.

futureDirections.title: Richer experience signals
futureDirections.body: Explore additional player, companion, and world-event signals while retaining a clear shared representation.

futureDirections.title: Broader character roles
futureDirections.body: Study how the shared model could support different companion roles and progression paths under authored constraints.

futureDirections.title: Player-facing explanation
futureDirections.body: Explore how a game could communicate why a companion changed through its accumulated experiences.

principle: A character's behaviour and abilities could become related outcomes of what it has experienced, while designers retain responsibility for the rules, constraints, and boundaries that make those outcomes understandable.
